summary.en: A point estimate is a single number computed from a sample to stand in for an unknown population parameter, but it is almost never exactly right; an interval estimate reports a range around it — built from the sample's own variability — that would contain the true parameter in a stated proportion of repeated samples, which is the honest way to communicate how much a point estimate can be trusted.
summary.et: Punkthinnang on üksainus arv, mis arvutatakse valimist tundmatu populatsiooniparameetri esindamiseks, kuid see on peaaegu mitte kunagi täpselt õige; vahemikhinnang esitab selle ümber vahemiku — mis on üles ehitatud valimi omast varieeruvusest —, mis sisaldaks tõelist parameetrit teatud osas korduvatest valimitest, ning see on aus viis öelda, kui palju punkthinnangut usaldada.
